output.interpretation: Case: hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) tumor tissue. Control: adjacent non-tumor liver tissue, from the same patients where the data allow. Both arms come from human surgical bulk RNA-seq series.

clarifying_questions.question: Should the analysis be limited to one HCC cause or patient population, or should it pool all of them?
options: HBV-related HCC (mostly Chinese/Asian cohorts, e.g. GSE56545, GSE124535, GSE138485)
HCV-related HCC (only GSE81550, which has 3 pairs, too small)
Non-Asian cohorts (GSE202853 Hispanic, GSE176271 African/European American, GSE144269 Mongolian)
clarifying_questions.why: About 18 paired tumor/adjacent series qualify, more than the 10 the analysis can take. Most series do not record the cause per sample, and the sample counts differ a lot between these options.

clarifying_questions.question: Should tumors from patients with venous invasion (PVTT), recurrence or immunotherapy be included, or only standard resected primary tumors?
clarifying_questions.why: This decides whether GSE69164 (stage III with PVTT), GSE56545 (transplant patients with or without recurrence) and GSE202069 (some patients given anti-PD-1) stay in.

rejected.why: Only 10 non-tumor samples against 68 tumors, and they are mostly unpaired.
The controls are normal liver from non-HCC patients plus premalignant lesions, not adjacent non-tumor liver.
Only 3 pairs (HCV). Usable only if the user wants HCV-specific data.
Only 4 pairs, and the series mixes in small-RNA libraries.
Only 6 samples, from a circRNA study.
Qualifies (9 pairs) but was left out because of the 10-candidate cap.
Qualifies (17 pairs, rRNA-depleted, some recurrent tumors) but was left out because of the 10-candidate cap.
too few samples with counts per arm (case 0, control 0; at least 3 each)

candidates.title: The genomic landscape of Mongolian hepatocellular carcinoma
candidates.why: The largest series found: 70 HCC tumors with matched non-tumor liver, all from surgery.
concerns: Mongolian cohort with high HBV/HDV prevalence; clinical data are held in dbGaP, not GEO.

candidates.title: A novel risk score based on immune-related genes for hepatocellular carcinoma as a reliable prognostic biomarker and correlated with immune infiltration
candidates.why: 65 HCC tumors with paired paracancerous liver.
concerns: Cause of HCC is not annotated.

candidates.title: Gene expression profiles of 35 paired HCC and non-tumor tissues by RNA-seq data
candidates.why: 35 early-stage HCC tumors with paired non-tumor liver.

candidates.title: Retrospective gene expression analysis of human RNA samples from Hepatocellular Carcinoma in relation with survival
candidates.why: 32 tumor/non-tumor pairs from the same patients.
concerns: Some non-tumor titles use a 'T_' prefix. The rule therefore matches on 'Non Tumor' in the title.
9 samples matched both arms and were set aside: ['GSM4184967', 'GSM4184968', 'GSM4184969', 'GSM4184970', 'GSM4184971']

candidates.title: RNA-seq data for tumor and adjacent non-tumor tissues from hepatocellular carcinoma patients with anti-PD-1 therapy
candidates.why: 41 resected HCC tumors and 25 adjacent non-tumor liver samples.
concerns: Pairing is incomplete. 17 samples are labelled with anti-PD-1 treatment, and the records do not say when it was given relative to surgery.

candidates.title: mRNA profiling  of Hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC)
candidates.why: 21 HBV-related HCC tumors, each paired with its adjacent normal liver, from transplant patients.
concerns: Transplant (OLT) cohort, mostly cirrhotic and HBV-positive.
6 selected samples are not in the NCBI count table

candidates.title: Integrative analysis of DNA methylation and microRNA expression reveals mechanisms of disparity in hepatocellular carcinoma [RNA-Seq]
candidates.why: 16 HCC tumors and 16 adjacent normal samples from a US cohort.
concerns: Race is split between African American and European American donors; consider it as a covariate.
4 selected samples are not in the NCBI count table

candidates.title: Comprehensive transcriptome analysis in human liver
candidates.why: 17 primary HCC tumors and 22 benign adjacent liver samples. Cell lines are excluded.
concerns: Some adjacent samples come from relapse cases, so not every control has a primary-tumor partner. The 5 relapse tumors are marked unclear.

candidates.title: Transcriptome analysis of hepatocellular carcinoma and adjacent non-tumor liver tissues [I]
candidates.why: 10 paired HCC/adjacent samples from Hispanic patients.
